In a fictional example, twenty of ten thousand babies have permanent loss.
The screen catches nineteen of them; sensitivity is ninety-five percent.
But four hundred healthy babies also fail the screen.
Only about four and a half percent of fails have true loss.
So a fail is not a diagnosis; it means further testing.
